title: story-card template variables
description: Values for templates/story-card.md.j2 and templates/story-card.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from story-card.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

activity.title: Activity
activity.description: Which backbone activity this sits under. If it does not obviously belong to one, either the backbone is wrong or this task is really two - both worth finding out before estimating.

observable_result.title: Observable result
observable_result.description: Given , when , then. From section 'Acceptance Criteria'.

persona.title: Persona
persona.description: The named persona this serves, from your persona set. "As a user" is the phrase that lets a card serve everyone and satisfy no one; name the person.

recovery_result.title: Recovery result
recovery_result.description: Given , when , then. From section 'Error/Recovery Path'.

release_slice.title: Release slice
release_slice.description: Which slice this card is in. walking-skeleton means the thinnest end-to-end path - if everything looks like it belongs there, nobody has yet been made to choose.

size.title: Size
size.description: Relative size from the people who will build it. An L or XL on a story map is usually a card that has not been split, and splitting it is the point of the map.

task_name.title: Task name
task_name.description: The task as it appears on the map, in the user's verb - "Upload receipt". Not a component name; a card named after a screen cannot be sliced out of a release.

user_action.title: User action
user_action.description: What they want to do, in their language and at their level of detail. Not the implementation - "attach a photo of the receipt", not "POST multipart to /receipts".
